docs.title: Awesome-Shiksha
docs.text:
I'm creating this page to dump all of my ideas about how an education system shall be and what it should be covered with teaching methodology. Feel free to read it, implement it with your known ones, and reach out to discuss anything relevant!

The purpose creating this page is to have accessible education for all with access to internet in proper consolidated way. The basic idea, in current education system, of having "board" exam in grade 10 is to check if student is ready to deep dive in specific studies. In other words, Do they have bare minimum knowledge to survive in real world, tackle real problems (not finding innovative solutions, just tackling problems only), and at least knows what different options they have to choose from! But I feel from current system most of the anaswer from above questions will be no even for grade 10 topper. and failure in grade 10 would have better exposure to real life problems. Mostly students still feel clueless in thier real life even after completing their undergrad level studies and don't know what do they want from their life. It's still okay to not knowing what do you want and you're figuring out by experimenting different stuffs that's actually better then following conventional ways of 9-5 jobs when you're not enjoying but staying still and having stagnant life and too much free time is where it all problems start: for individual, for their families, and for a society. So, I wanted to design an educational plan / informal curriculum that covers most of the basics that I feel if I would have known earlier, I would be the different person, not as an academic / career wise but as an human!

  • A plan that not only makes an individual a self reliant but improves overall us a society, as a nation.

  • A structure that can be used by any parents to homeschool their kids or for any eacher if they want to go extra mile for their students from conventional curriculum.

  • A methodology that develops scientific temparament, curious minds, respects new ideas including the ones that may not lie withing the same ideology, and rational thinking.

docs.title: How to use this project!
docs.text: • This project is designed in modular way!

docs.title: Raise a Issue for new feature / content
docs.text:
• If you could not find what you're looking for: Raise a issues with as detailed explanation and we'll try to add it as soon as possible! Follow below template to provide information:
    • Target grade / Age group
    • Subject
    • Topic
    • [ Optional ] Suggested methodology

With saying all of that, there can be flaws in any suggestions that I made, but conisdering a little to no experience in teaching, I could be wrong at any point or very much optimistic but I want to have "OUR" plan and not my plan so feel free to reach out to me for any kind of feedback, and constuctive discussion. Contributions are more than welcome!

docs.title: Where content lives
docs.text:
Content is organized by age group, and within each age group, by subject:

docs/
├── 3-5-years/     (Pre-School)
├── 6-9-years/      (Grade 1 to 4)
├── 10-13-years/    (Grade 5 to 8)
├── 14-15-years/    (Grade 9 to 10)
│   ├── README.md    <- overview / subject index for this age group
│   ├── maths.md
│   ├── science.md
│   ├── english.md
│   └── ethics.md

Each subject page (e.g. docs/6-9-years/maths.md) holds all topics for that subject and age group. Add a new topic as a ## section within the relevant subject page — don't create a new file per topic.

If you want to add a subject that doesn't exist yet for an age group (e.g. history.md), create the file following the same pattern, link it from that age group's README.md, and add it to mkdocs.yaml's nav:.

Basic idea is each topic shall be planned as per time required to finish. Do not plan anything larger than 1 hour. Follow below idea to design topic, follwing this template is must:

  1. Objective Why is this topic important and shall be taught? What learning outcome will be achieved after completing it?
  2. Methodology: There can be any kind of method to be followed to achieve the objective. It could be youtube video, blog, movie, short-films, documentary, specific book chapter, or you can be creative and add your own ideas of how it shall be taught!
  3. Exercise [ Optional] : Basically homeworks. Focus on quality over quantity here. For example: More difficult task that requires original thinking than number of easy tasks!
  4. Evaluation Criteria: Be Creative here. Not every topic /subject can be evaluated with same pen/paper based written examination. Main idea of this project is to to prepare students to tackle real life challanges and how basic education can help help them to become better overall human being along with useful skills. For example, Topics of history like on world wars and freedom fighters life could not be evaluated by asking them to rewrite history word-to-word as they memorize it! It can be planned as something like group discussions with topics of why it happened, what do they think what went wrong, what could have prevented it, etc. At this point, it's also needed to undestand not each evaluation criteria can be measured in quantitative ways. It can be qualitative as well. In short, be creative and be relevant.
  5. Contributor: [ Optional ] If you like to add your name and contact / e-mail details here, in case if someone would like to reach out to you.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
Every subject page starts with a tags: frontmatter block, e.g.:

---
tags:
  - maths
  - 6-9-years
---

Keep the subject and age-group tags already on the page, and add more as relevant to help visitors filter content on the site's Tags page — for example video, exercise, group-activity, or a specific topic name like fractions. Tags are site-wide, so reuse existing tags where they fit instead of inventing near-duplicates (check ../tags.md after building the site).

Once you submit your PR (refer below to understand how it's done), We (hoping adding more volunteers in future) would review it and if it is matching with the current ideology of this project, it will be merged into this main branch and will add your name in contributor's list after 3(!?) contributions. If we feel, PR is not matching with current ideology, or there's chance of improvement in any way, it will be mentioned in that PR specific discussion on github.

Lastly, If you want to contribute but have no idea from where to start, then refer issues page and pick any open issues and get started! Happy Learning :)

docs.title: Technical Understanding requirement
docs.text:
This website is created based on Python with mkdocs. Related page are written in markdown files.

I'm planning that any person not familiar to coding environment can also contribute to this project. So, listing out below necessary materials one should refer before starting out.

  • Refer this to know more on how markdown files should be written and its features.

  • Refer blog to know how you can setup similiar webpage for your project or setup this repo in your computer to contributing this project.

  • Learn about basics of git that will be used to add more content from various contributor.

docs.title: Follow these steps to setup environment on your computer
docs.text:
1. Set up github account
    • Install git
    • Create a github account
    • In your command line terminal type below commands:
    • Use SSH so you don't need to type password. Follow each steps in provided link.
git config --global user.name "Your Name"
git config --global user.email "you@example.com"
# Windows tip: avoid line-ending noise
git config --global core.autocrlf input
  1. Fork and Clone Awesome-Shiksha
    • Click Fork on GitHub
    • Clone forked project in your computer.
# If SSH not setup
git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/Awesome-Shiksha.git
# With SSH
git@github.com:<your-username>/Awesome-Shiksha.git
cd Awesome-Shiksha
  1. Create a branch and add all of your stuff there!
git checkout -b <topic>/short-desc
# examples: maths/calculus, science/grade8
  • Write what ever you want to add
  • Add commit
  • Push to remote
git add <files> or git add .
git commit -m "added pythagorus theorem"
git push
  1. Open a Pull Request (PR)
    • Go to your account on github and open this repo.
    • Click Compare & Pull Request
